claims.text: Deep cryogenic treatment can be applied as a post-processing step after laser additive manufacturing of a BCC Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr high-entropy alloy.
The deep cryogenic treatment involves cooling to approximately -196 °C and subsequently returning the component to room temperature.
As-deposited laser-additively manufactured HEA components exhibit residual stresses.
As-deposited laser-additively manufactured HEA components exhibit microstructural heterogeneity.
As-deposited laser-additively manufactured HEA components contain fabrication defects.
Deep cryogenic treatment induces a phase transition in laser-deposited Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr HEA without requiring additional deformation.
Deep cryogenic treatment refines the grains of additively manufactured HEAs.
Deep cryogenic treatment reduces residual stress in additively manufactured HEAs.
Deep cryogenic treatment may induce beneficial nanotwinning in additively manufactured HEAs.
Phase transitions and changes to defect structures caused by DCT produce a more uniform microstructure.
Stress relief and greater grain uniformity reduce dimensional distortion.
Nanotwinning and other dislocation mechanisms improve mechanical properties by mitigating fabrication-induced defects.
DCT-treated components will have better dimensional precision than untreated as-deposited components.
DCT-treated components will have a lower density of pores and other fabrication defects than untreated components.
DCT treatment increases tensile strength relative to the as-deposited Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy.
DCT treatment increases tensile elongation relative to the as-deposited Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy.
The reported DCT-treated alloy has 11% higher tensile strength and 10% higher elongation than the as-deposited alloy.
The benefits of DCT may extend from the studied Hf-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy to HEAs with similar compositions and BCC crystal structures.
DCT efficacy may be limited in alloys with substantially different phase behavior or when treatment parameters are not optimized.
The long-term effect of DCT on fatigue and other service properties across HEA systems remains uncertain.
